question.text: During a SIAB hearing into alleged professional misconduct by an empanelled SIA, the aggrieved SIA is entitled to:

answer.text: Written charges, a fair hearing, the right to lead evidence, the right to cross-examine witnesses and the right to be represented by a qualified professional.
A private in-camera hearing only if the charges relate to money-laundering, otherwise the SIA has no right to personal appearance.
A 7-day hearing window with no right to lead evidence - only to submit a written reply.
Only a right to submit a written reply; the SIAB panel's determination is ex-parte by default.

explanation.text: The Logic: Quasi-judicial disciplinary hearings — including those conducted by SIAB-type bodies — are governed by principles of natural justice. These principles entitle the aggrieved party to written charges (audi alteram partem), a fair hearing, the right to lead evidence, the right to cross-examine adverse witnesses, and the right to be represented by counsel or a qualified peer professional. The Trap: Ex-parte default proceedings, reply-only processes that deny oral hearing, and narrow in-camera rules each defeat natural justice. SIAB is not an informal committee but a quasi-judicial disciplinary body. Note: The specific SIAB-hearing entitlements (written charges, right to lead evidence, cross-examination, qualified-professional representation) are not enumerated in the cited Social Impact Assessors Certification Examination Workbook (January 2026) pages 113-114, 124, 126, 138 or 213, which cover general SIA competence/evidence/reporting, SRO empanelment and general SEBI penalties. The framing above reflects general regulatory/natural-justice principles applied in disciplinary jurisprudence.
